Subject: SIG follow-ups: SCIM role mapping / delegated admin concerns

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the initial SIG workbook — we've reviewed and had a couple of follow-up asks specifically around access controls before we sign off:

1) Delegated admin boundaries: can you confirm how Redwood prevents a delegated admin (SAML group-mapped role) from elevating privileges across tenants or to other admin roles? Any guardrails or admin-only APIs that are blocked?

2) SCIM role mapping: we need to map our internal roles very granularly. Does Redwood support role filters or attribute-based mapping so we can map groups to a scoped non-admin role (e.g., "app_readonly_payment_ops") rather than to a site-admin? Any example mappings would help.

3) MFA and service accounts: can you confirm the MFA posture for service accounts and whether you enforce re-auth or step-up for sensitive actions (role changes, billing)?

I've attached our follow-up sheet with specific question numbers. Would appreciate short answers we can include back into our SIG deliverable. If it's easier to discuss, we can book a 20-minute call this week.

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Marissa will add technical detail on SCIM/RBAC. Happy to walk through over a quick call. Proposed times: Tue 10/13 10:00am PT or Wed 10/14 2:00pm PT.

1) Delegated admin boundaries: Redwood enforces tenant-scoped role resolution. SAML group-to-role mappings are evaluated per-tenant; there is no cross-tenant role inheritance. Admin-level APIs require both (a) an admin role AND (b) a scoped tenant context. We also require an additional approval step for role escalations when the request originates from a token created via a service integration.

2) SCIM role mapping: SCIM supports attribute and group-based mapping with filters. You can map a group to any predefined role (including custom scoped roles). We attach a simple RBAC matrix showing recommended mappings.

3) MFA & service accounts: We rely on the IdP for primary authentication and MFA enforcement. For critical admin actions (role changes, delete org, billing changes), Redwood enforces a step-up policy that can be configured to require reauthentication or to require an allowlist of IPs. Service accounts use short-lived tokens with automatic rotation; we can additionally require that service account token issuance be tied to a specific service principal and audited (see attachment).

Next steps: I attached a short RBAC matrix and a Drive link with the SCIM role-filter example. If the times above work, I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda focusing on (a) SCIM mapping, (b) delegated admin guardrails, and (c) audit evidence you requested.

Best,

Laura — adding the technical detail you asked for so you can include it verbatim in the SIG response. Happy to jump on the call as well.

SCIM / Role mapping (detailed):
- We support SCIM 2.0 push provisioning. Roles are created in Redwood as role templates (system roles or custom templates). SCIM mappings can be: group -> role, attribute -> role, or filter -> role.
- Role filters: you can use SCIM expressions (e.g., members:contains("group:payments-ops") AND externalId=="acme-prod") to limit when a mapping applies. This is how you can ensure a group only maps to a scoped non-admin role in the production tenant.
- Admin elevation guardrails:
  - Mapping to any admin (site-admin, org-admin) requires an "admin-approval" flag in the provisioning flow; if flagged, the initial provision will create the user in a pending state and send an approval request to a configurable set of approvers.
  - Built-in safe-guards block SCIM from granting cross-tenant admin roles: the mapping evaluation includes tenant context.

MFA / service accounts:
- For interactive users we recommend IdP-enforced MFA (we honor standard SAML MFA assertions).
- For non-interactive/service accounts: tokens are short-lived (default 4 hours) and rotated automatically. Sensitive admin APIs require either (a) a token created from an interactive, MFA-authenticated session or (b) a service principal on a pre-approved allowlist with recorded justification.

Least-privilege guidance:
- Create custom scoped roles for integration (e.g., app_readonly_payment_ops). Use SCIM filters to map only the specific groups that need access.
- For billing and org-level actions require both role AND a secondary approval check in the Console (or via API with a flagged justification).

Attachments: sample SCIM filter and a JSON snippet showing a scoped mapping.
